title: Tamsin and the Songbook
premise: Dominic Fairweather has spent ten years writing anonymous letters to Tamsin Vale, the vineyard heiress he loved and lost, signing them only 'The Songbook' after the mixtape they once shared. When Tamsin returns to the valley to save her family's failing winery—and moves into the flat beside his struggling café—she begins hunting the letter-writer while falling for the gruff pastry chef next door, never suspecting they are the same man. As her ruthless fiancé Marcus maneuvers to seize the vineyard and Dominic's café faces foreclosure, Tamsin discovers his identity at the worst possible moment, feeling a decade of devotion was also a decade of deception. At the vineyard's first harvest festival, Dominic must publicly claim both his letters and his love, choosing truth over safety, and Tamsin must choose the imperfect real man over the perfect paper ghost—ending with them pressing the season's first bottles together, labeled with lyrics from their song.
about_author: August Reyes is the pen name of a former line cook who spent six years working café kitchens in wine country before turning to fiction. They write love stories about people who express themselves better through craft than conversation.

chapters.title: The Last Payment Notice
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A foreclosure warning arrives at Flour & Salt café on the same morning Dominic mails his 120th anonymous letter to Tamsin Vale. He tells himself the letters are closure, not hope. Emotional beat: weary self-deception, establishing what he stands to lose.

chapters.title: Moving Vans and Merlot
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. After her father's stroke, Tamsin leaves London and her engagement to investor Marcus Hale, moving into the cottage beside Dominic's café. She recognizes the valley instantly; she doesn't yet recognize the man waving awkwardly over the fence. Beat: reluctant homecoming.

chapters.title: Flour on His Hands
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin wanders into the café seeking coffee and finds pastries that taste uncannily like the ones from her youth—including a tart she's only ever described in her replies to The Songbook. Suspicion flickers; Dominic deflects. Beat: first crack of mystery.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus arrives unannounced with a restructuring plan that would sell half the Vale vineyard to cover debts. Tamsin resists; Marcus reminds her of promises made. Beat: duty tightening like a noose, villain established sympathetically at first.

chapters.title: The Songbook Letters
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Alone, Tamsin rereads a decade of letters and resolves to find their author now that she lives one valley away. She notices the letters always mention local details—bakery hours, harvest weather. Beat: the hunt begins, tenderness mixed with resolve.

chapters.title: Sourdough Diplomacy
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic offers Tamsin a trade: bread for her surplus fruit, keeping her close under practical pretense. Their banter rekindles old ease, terrifying him. Beat: proximity as danger, warmth he can't afford.

chapters.title: Vineyard Audit
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Going through her father's books, Tamsin finds the vineyard deeper in debt than admitted—and finds Marcus's name already on two loan guarantees. Beat: the trap's shape becomes visible; loyalty to family vs. suspicion of fiancé.

chapters.title: A Letter, Answered
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic mails letter 121, then panics realizing Tamsin can now trace details too easily. He considers stopping—but writing to her is the only place he's honest. Beat: addiction to the lie, guilt sharpening.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tamsin short-staffed before an early harvest begs Dominic's help; he works the vines beside her, hands blistering, heart exposed. A near-kiss interrupted by Marcus's call. Beat: longing against obligation.

chapters.title: The Café Inspector
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A surprise health inspection—anonymous complaint—threatens Dominic's license. He suspects Marcus clearing the commercial space for a boutique tasting room. Beat: power flexing its corruption; stakes turn physical.

chapters.title: Postmark Clues
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Comparing postmarks, Tamsin narrows The Songbook to this town. She starts testing neighbors with casual mentions that would bait a reply. Beat: detective romance energy; dramatic irony tightens around Dominic.

chapters.title: What Marcus Knows
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus has discovered the letters exist via a private investigator and plans to use them—framing the writer as a stalker—to force Tamsin back to London and full control of the sale. Beat: antagonist weaponizes intimacy.

chapters.title: Night Harvest
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Racing a storm, the crew picks through the night. Soaked and laughing, Dominic and Tamsin finally kiss in the cellar among the barrels. Beat: peak romance midpoint; joy with a shadow behind it.

chapters.title: The Morning After the Storm
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Bliss curdles: Tamsin mentions her fiancé, her duty, her leaving when the harvest ends. Dominic realizes he's lent pieces of himself again instead of the whole. Beat: emotional retreat, self-aware cowardice.

chapters.title: Letter 122, Unsent
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic writes a confession letter and seals it, unable to send or destroy it. He hides it inside the old songbook cassette case. Beat: the truth physically present but locked away—a Chekhov object planted.

chapters.title: Shareholder Meeting
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin stalls the vineyard sale by invoking her grandmother's charter requiring a harvest-festival vote. Buys time; enrages Marcus. Beat: agency reclaimed through heritage—love of land vs. deal-making.

chapters.title: Café Full of Neighbors
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The town rallies with a benefit night at Flour & Salt, buying out the pastry case to cover arrears. Dominic, who kept everyone at arm's length, is undone by being seen. Beat: community as mirror—he preaches invisibility, receives belonging.

chapters.title: The Investigator's Photos
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The PI photographs Dominic mailing a letter. Marcus now holds proof and schedules his reveal for maximum damage—the festival eve. Beat: clock starts ticking; reader knows what characters don't.

chapters.title: Recipe for Two
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin cooks with Dominic using a recipe from a Songbook letter; he corrects a detail only the writer could know. She says nothing, heart hammering. Beat: near-revelation; she chooses to wait, wanting him to volunteer truth.

chapters.title: Duty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin weighs honoring her engagement promise against feelings for Dominic, examining whether loyalty to a promise made under pressure is virtue or cage. Beat: theme crystallized—loyalty vs. truth.

chapters.title: Foreclosure Friday
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The bank declines the benefit's partial payment; the café gets thirty days. Dominic, humiliated, almost signs Marcus's buyout offer—which includes a gag clause about 'correspondence.' Beat: temptation to disappear permanently.

chapters.title: The Cassette
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Helping Dominic pack fragile stock, Tamsin finds the old songbook cassette—and the unsent confession inside. She reads it alone. Beat: revelation. Grief and fury entwined: ten years of love, ten years of hiding.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Fence
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tamsin confronts Dominic: why write if you'd never sign? He answers with the whole truth—poverty, shame, the belief she'd outgrown him. She calls it cowardice dressed as devotion. Beat: all-is-lost rupture.

chapters.title: London Calling
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus presents Tamsin the PI file, reframing Dominic as a decade-long stalker, and demands she return to London immediately. Tamsin sees the manipulation but the poison lands anyway. Beat: villain's triumph, doubt weaponized.

chapters.title: Empty Kitchen
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic stops baking, boxes the café early, drafts a goodbye letter he doesn't send. His mentor Rosa forces him to admit he's repeating his mother's pattern: leaving before being left. Beat: rock bottom, insight earned.

chapters.title: Reading the Whole Decade
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin rereads every letter chronologically and watches the writer grow braver across ten years—watching him become someone worth loving in ink. She compares the letters to Marcus's polished lies. Beat: judgment shifts; truth vs. performance.

chapters.title: Rosa's Testimony
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV (brief). Rosa visits Tamsin, telling the story of the boy who wrote letters to a girl leaving, and the man who fed the town when no one fed him. Beat: external validation; bridge between the lovers.

chapters.title: The Charter Clause
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin discovers Marcus falsified loan documents to trigger the forced sale. With her lawyer aunt, she prepares to expose him at the festival vote. Beat: plot engine reignites; justice aligned with heart.

chapters.title: Thirty Days, Day Twenty-Nine
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Final notice day. Instead of surrendering, Dominic bakes through the night—harvest tarts for the festival, betting everything on one public act. Beat: courage chosen before confidence arrives.

chapters.title: Festival Eve Sabotage
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Marcus's team tampers with the festival's power and spreads the 'stalker' story to townsfolk. Dominic hears the whispers and understands what tomorrow will cost. Beat: darkness before dawn; reputation on the block.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the harvest assembly, Tamsin presents the forged documents; the town votes down the sale. Marcus, cornered, plays his card: he announces the letters and names Dominic. Beat: public detonation of the secret.

chapters.title: Whole Heart, Whole Voice
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Called before the crowd, Dominic doesn't deny it. He reads Letter One aloud—written at nineteen, broke and terrified—then claims every year since, and asks for nothing. Beat: climax; truth offered without demand.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Means
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin publicly releases herself from the engagement—not because Marcus lied about Dominic, but because she finally distinguishes loyalty to a person from obedience to a bargain. Beat: thematic resolution of duty vs. love.

chapters.title: Marcus Exits
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Facing fraud exposure, Marcus negotiates quiet withdrawal rather than prosecution, revealing a flicker of the man he might have been before deals replaced people. Beat: villain humanized, threat dissolved.

chapters.title: The First Pour
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Days later, Dominic and Tamsin taste the new vintage in the cellar—awkward, tender, rebuilding trust brick by brick. She gives him the cassette; he gives her Letter 123, signed with his name. Beat: reconciliation begun honestly.

chapters.title: Lease Renewed
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. With the vineyard partnership secured—Flour & Salt supplying the tasting room—the café survives. Dominic signs a lease for the first time without flinching. Beat: material stakes resolved as symbols of commitment.

chapters.title: Meeting the Father
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin introduces Dominic to her recovering father, who reveals he always suspected The Songbook and kept one letter framed. Blessing given with gruff humor. Beat: family healed, generational echo closed.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival, Again
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The town's belated festival: Dominic's tarts, Tamsin's wine, dancing under string lights where the whisper campaign once lived. The town apologizes in the best way—by showing up. Beat: communal restoration.

chapters.title: Label Lyrics
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Bottling day: Tamsin labels the first cuvée with a lyric from their song, crediting 'D. Fairweather, correspondent.' Dominic watches his name in print and keeps it there. Beat: identity claimed, love made public and permanent.

chapters.title: Letter 124, Signed
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Epilogue: Dominic writes one last letter and hand-delivers it across the fence—no envelope needed anymore. It's a proposal written the way he's always told the truth: slowly, specifically, entirely hers. Beat: full-circle resolution; the past tense becomes future.
